results.question: Which valves must be closed to isolate T4750 for maintenance? List them in the order you would close them, explain the order, and say which connections this drawing does not let you isolate.
results.answer:
Facts in the drawing
- T4750 (Tank-1), Tank [E1.1]

Derived by graph analysis of the drawing
- GlobeValve 47123/C1 (GlobeValve-2) is the first valve on the upstream side of T4750 (Tank-1) (line 47123, DN 80) [E2.2, isolation_boundary]
- GlobeValve 47127/C1 (GlobeValve-1) is the first valve on the upstream side of T4750 (Tank-1) (line 47127, DN 50) [E2.3, isolation_boundary]
- ButterflyValve 47124/C1 (ButterflyValve-1) is the first valve on the downstream side of T4750 (Tank-1) (line 47124, DN 80) [E2.4, isolation_boundary]
- SV 104.01 (SpringLoadedGlobeSafetyValve-1) discharges into the piping around T4750 (Tank-1) with no valve in between (line 47125, DN 50); it does not relieve this region [E2.5, isolation_boundary]

Not established by the P&ID
- Not represented in the drawing: The P&ID does not provide the tag names for these valves; only their line/component identifiers are shown.

Summary (model wording; the lists above are what was checked)
To isolate tank T4750 for maintenance, close the two upstream valves first (GlobeValve 47123/C1 on line 47123 and GlobeValve 47127/C1 on line 47127), then close the downstream valve (ButterflyValve 47124/C1 on line 47124). This order stops inflow, then outflow, allowing safe depressurization. The drawing does not allow isolation of the connection to the safety valve SV 104.01 on line 47125, as there is no valve between the tank and that relief device.
